title: Magnetoelectric Phase Transition and Axion Dynamics
authors: Chen-Hui Xie, Runyu Lei, Jiayi Liu, Yihuai Chen, Jinxing Zhang, Yu Gao, Sichun Sun
abstract: Magnetoelectric phase transitions have been experimentally studied, but no macroscopic theory has been proposed to explain their dynamical origin. In this work, we assume that the axion quasiparticle with frequency undergoes a condensation like process. We show that these magnetoelectric phase transitions can be described within a Ginzbur Landau framework by introducing a coupled dynamic parameter, the axion angle, which is proportional to the magnetoelectric coeffcient. We derive relations between the static axion angle, the axion frequency, and the phase transition temperature for different magnetoelectric materials, respectively, and compare these calculations with existing experimental results. We also connect the artificially designed Dzyaloshinskii Moriya interaction with the axion condensate like process, so that the relation between the static axion angle and the experimentally measured frequency shift can be obtained.
summary: This work proposes that magnetoelectric phase transitions are governed by the condensation-like dynamics of an axion quasiparticle. By applying an extended Ginzburg-Landau framework analogous to BEC theory, the authors derive quantitative relationships linking the static axion angle, the transition temperature, and the material's intrinsic coupling strengths. This provides a novel, unified theoretical description for understanding ME effects.
main_problem: To develop a macroscopic theory explaining the dynamical origin of magnetoelectric (ME) phase transitions, which are experimentally observed but lack a comprehensive theoretical framework.
main_result: The ME phase transition can be successfully modeled by treating the axion quasiparticle (AQ) field as undergoing a Bose-Einstein Condensation (BEC)-like process, yielding scaling laws between the static AQ angle and the transition temperature.
method: The authors employ an extended Ginzburg-Landau (GL) theory, linearizing the equations of motion around the critical temperature and analyzing the resulting dynamics in the frequency domain.
model_or_system: The system involves coupled dynamics of magnetization (M), polarization (P), and the axion angle ($	heta$) in ME materials, modeled using a free energy functional and incorporating concepts from Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI).
key_observables: Static AQ angle ($	heta_0$), AQ frequency ($\omega_a$), and the ME phase transition temperature ($T_c$).
important_parameters: Phenomenological coefficients ($\lambda_M, \lambda_	heta$), damping coefficients ($\eta_M, \eta_P$), and the DMI strength ($D$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on phenomenological damping terms inserted by hand, the assumption of spatially homogeneous solutions, and treating the AQ dynamics as a weakly interacting Bose gas.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the relationship between the AQ angle and temperature, showing power-law scaling ($	heta_0 \propto T_c^{3/4}$) that fits experimental data, and depict the BEC phase diagram.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the ME coupling, formulating the dynamics via GL theory, deriving the BEC analogy for the AQ field, and finally deriving quantitative relationships between $	heta_0$, $\omega_a$, and $T_c$ by solving the linearized equations of motion.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between the critical dynamics of a condensed matter phase transition (ME transition) and the universal physics of BEC provides a powerful, unifying theoretical lens for understanding emergent quantum phenomena in solids.
